docs.title: Aegis Security Hub
docs.text:
Cybersecurity Assessment | Risk Management | Detection | Incident Response

Welcome to the Aegis Security Hub.

This website presents the security assessment, defensive controls, risk register, detection results and incident response documentation developed as part of the Aegis Shield cybersecurity learning project.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text: Aegis Shield is a cybersecurity learning project focused on identifying security weaknesses, reviewing secure coding practices, protecting audit records, detecting suspicious activities and preparing incident response procedures.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Aegis Shield includes a Python-based detection and monitoring learning exercise using synthetic authentication, payroll audit and web request datasets.

docs.title: Assessment Results
docs.text: Data Source Events Analysed Authentication logs 11,487 Payroll audit events 2,652 Web requests 5,805 Total 19,944

docs.title: Detection Categories
docs.text:
The assessment included detection logic for:

  • Repeated authentication failures.
  • Password spraying indicators.
  • Unusual authentication patterns.
  • Administrative activity outside expected hours.
  • Sensitive payroll access and export activity.
  • Suspicious web request patterns.
  • Potential injection and scanning indicators.

docs.title: Alert Summary
docs.text:
The recorded assessment produced 21 alert rows across the configured detection rules.

Alerts require human investigation. They are indicators for review, not proof that an attack or data breach occurred.

docs.title: Three Things Never to Publish
docs.text:
1. Passwords, API keys and private keys: They could allow unauthorised access.
  2. Real personal or customer information: It could expose private information.
  3. Detailed exploit instructions and vulnerable system configurations: They could help someone attack systems.

The public Security Hub is a learning portfolio, not a production security environment.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Aegis Shield is a cybersecurity assessment and defensive monitoring learning project.

The project demonstrates security assessment, secure code review, audit logging, risk management, detection engineering and incident response documentation.

docs.title: 1. Security Assessment
docs.text: Reviewed application security weaknesses and documented findings with supporting evidence and limitations.

docs.title: 2. Secure Code Review
docs.text: Used Bandit, Semgrep, Gitleaks and OSV-Scanner to review code and identify security concerns.

docs.title: 3. Audit Logging
docs.text: Implemented hash-chain verification to demonstrate detection of changes to audit records.

docs.title: 4. Attack Detection
docs.text: Developed Python-based detection logic to identify suspicious authentication, payroll and web activity in assessment datasets.

docs.title: 5. Incident Response
docs.text: Prepared playbooks for payroll data breaches, ransomware incidents and insider salary disclosure scenarios.

docs.title: 6. Risk Management
docs.text: Created a risk register containing 17 risks and a compliance mapping covering 14 security controls.

docs.title: Project Limitations
docs.text:
• Assessment data is synthetic.
  • Static analysis results do not prove complete application security.
  • Detection alerts require human investigation.
  • The project does not represent live production monitoring.
  • Some remediation and validation activities remain pending.

docs.title: Overall Outcome
docs.text:
The project provides documented evidence of practical cybersecurity learning across assessment, detection, risk management and incident response.

This is a fictional training project, not a certified security audit or compliance assessment.

docs.title: 7. Remediation Sprint (Task 18)
docs.text:
Completed isolated remediation demonstrations for payroll export authorization, salary-record access and employee-record ownership. All 20 associated regression tests passed.

Reviewed authentication detection evidence and updated an isolated eight-package dependency set. The scoped OSV scan reported zero vulnerability records after remediation, and pip check reported no broken requirements.

These results are limited to the demonstration environment and scoped package list. Production integration, MFA and rate-limiting verification, application-level testing and system-owner approval remain pending.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This section summarises security weaknesses identified during the Aegis Shield learning assessment.

The findings are based on source-code review and controlled laboratory assessment. They do not establish successful exploitation of a live system.

docs.title: Finding 1 – SQL Injection Risk
docs.text:
Category: Injection

Observation: Unsafe SQL query construction using string interpolation was identified during source-code review.

Potential Impact: Improper query handling may expose application data.

Recommended Mitigation: - Use parameterised queries. - Validate input on the server. - Apply least-privilege database permissions. - Include security tests in development.

Validation Status: Source-code issue identified. Runtime exploitation was not demonstrated.

docs.title: Finding 2 – Cross-Site Scripting Risk
docs.text:
Category: Injection / Client-side security

Observation: Unsafe HTML rendering patterns involving trusted HTML handling were identified.

Potential Impact: Improper handling of untrusted content may create a client-side scripting risk.

Recommended Mitigation: - Use framework-provided safe rendering. - Avoid bypassing sanitisation. - Apply context-appropriate output encoding. - Review untrusted HTML handling.

Validation Status: Unsafe rendering behaviour was observed. JavaScript execution was not demonstrated.

docs.title: Finding 3 – Broken Access Control Risk
docs.text:
Category: Access Control

Observation: A source-code review identified a potentially incomplete ownership check in basket retrieval logic.

Potential Impact: Inadequate ownership enforcement could expose another user's records.

Recommended Mitigation: - Enforce server-side ownership checks. - Apply deny-by-default access controls. - Review authorisation at every sensitive endpoint. - Add access-control tests.

Validation Status: Potential weakness identified through source review. Cross-user access was not tested.

docs.title: Assessment Limitations
docs.text:
• Findings are based on the available assessment evidence.
  • Successful exploitation was not established for these findings.
  • The findings do not represent a live production security audit.
  • Further authorised testing and remediation validation are required.

All assessment findings belong to a fictional cybersecurity learning project.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Aegis Shield includes three incident response playbooks prepared for cybersecurity learning and tabletop exercises.

docs.title: 1. Payroll Data Breach
docs.text:
Objective: Provide a structured response to suspected unauthorised payroll data access or disclosure.

Response priorities: - Validate the alert and identify the affected records. - Preserve relevant audit evidence. - Escalate to the appropriate security and payroll owners. - Follow authorised containment and recovery procedures. - Review access controls and export approvals.

docs.title: 2. Ransomware Incident
docs.text:
Objective: Document an organisational response approach for a suspected ransomware incident.

Response priorities: - Escalate the incident to the security response team. - Follow approved isolation and business continuity procedures. - Preserve relevant evidence. - Assess recovery readiness. - Review backup and security controls.

docs.title: 3. Insider Salary Disclosure
docs.text:
Objective: Address suspected inappropriate access to or disclosure of salary information.

Response priorities: - Review relevant access and audit records. - Preserve evidence and document findings. - Escalate through the approved organisational process. - Review authorisation and data protection controls. - Record corrective actions.

This section presents the security policy documentation prepared as part of the Aegis Shield learning project.

The policy pack covers security governance and practical control recommendations.

docs.title: Policy Areas
docs.text:
The policy documentation covers:

  1. Access Control Policy
  2. Password and Authentication Policy
  3. Data Protection Policy
  4. Acceptable Use Policy
  5. Secure Development Policy
  6. Vulnerability Management Policy
  7. Logging and Monitoring Policy
  8. Incident Response Policy
  9. Backup and Recovery Policy

docs.title: Policy Objectives
docs.text:
• Protect sensitive information.
  • Restrict access based on business requirements.
  • Encourage secure software development.
  • Identify and address security weaknesses.
  • Maintain appropriate security records.
  • Support consistent incident response.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Aegis Shield risk register consolidates 17 identified security risks using a likelihood and impact scoring method.

Scoring formula: Likelihood × Impact

docs.title: Risk Rating Scale
docs.text: Score Rating 1–4 Low 5–9 Medium 10–14 High 15–25 Critical

docs.title: Top Five Risks
docs.text: Risk ID Risk Description Likelihood Impact Score Rating R-01 Full payroll export risk 4 5 20 Critical R-02 Insider salary disclosure 4 5 20 Critical R-06 Repeated failed login activity 4 4 16 Critical R-14 Unremediated dependency advisories 4 4 16 Critical R-03 Incomplete ownership checks 3 5 15 Critical

docs.title: R-01 – Full Payroll Export Risk
docs.text: Recommended action: Review export authorisation, restrict access and strengthen approval controls.

docs.title: R-02 – Insider Salary Disclosure
docs.text: Recommended action: Apply least privilege, monitor sensitive data access and strengthen audit reviews.

docs.title: R-06 – Repeated Failed Login Activity
docs.text: Recommended action: Monitor authentication events and review account protection controls.

docs.title: R-14 – Dependency Advisories
docs.text: Recommended action: Review affected dependencies, prioritise remediation and perform a fresh vulnerability scan.

docs.title: R-03 – Incomplete Ownership Checks
docs.text: Recommended action: Enforce server-side ownership validation and review access-control logic.

docs.title: Remaining validation
docs.text:
1. Integrate authorization demonstrations with trusted production identity, role and approval services.
  2. Verify MFA enforcement and rate limiting through approved configuration and testing.
  3. Run application-level regression and security tests after dependency updates.
  4. Validate audit logging, retention and access protection.
  5. Obtain system-owner review and approval.

Risk closure rule: These five risks remain open until the relevant production controls are implemented, independently validated and formally accepted by the responsible risk owners. Passing isolated demonstration tests alone does not close a production risk.
